b007:
• Pote tout dokiman ou yo: bilten, sètifika, atestasyon, kanè — nan nenpòt lang, menm foto nan telefòn.
  • Lekòl la evalye yo epi li ka bay kredi pou klas ou te pase: matematik, syans, syans sosyal, epi premye lang ou konte kòm kredi lang etranje.
  • Klas 7yèm–8yèm ane yo (fen fondamantal an Ayiti) anjeneral koresponn ak middle school; apati 9yèm ane (segondè) ka bay kredi high school.
  • Pa gen dokiman? Y ap toujou mete w nan klas selon laj ou, epi nan kèk matyè ou ka pran yon egzamen pou jwenn kredi. Mande.
  • Mande evalyasyon an alekri epi kenbe yon kopi. Si yon kredi manke, mande konseye a pou l revize l ak pwofesè EL la.

b013: Newcomer note: a student can attend public high school until age 21 in Mississippi, so a 5-year plan is allowed and often wise for students who arrive at 16–17 with little English. Ask the counselor about it in 9th or 10th grade, not senior year. Ou ka ale lekòl jiska 21 an; yon plan 5 ane posib — mande bonè.
b014: Seal of Biliteracy · So Alfabetizasyon Bileng: Mississippi puts a seal on the diploma of students who show proficiency in English and another language. English counts with an ELPT score of 4 in all domains, English II test score of 4, ACT English 18, SAT 320 or AP English 3; the other language with AP (3), AAPPL or STAMP Intermediate-Mid (I4/L4) in all four skills, or a portfolio for languages without a test. Your home language is an asset — ask the counselor in 10th or 11th grade.
